title: Histopathological Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for Cancer Diagnosis and Gleason Grading: A Brief Review of Prostate Cancer.
source: PubMed · Journal of clinical practice and research
desc: [Journal of clinical practice and research] Prostate cancer, one of the most common cancers affecting men's health worldwide, ranks second among cancer-related deaths. Therefore, it represents a critical health issue, and early diagnosis is crucial. Several imaging and analytical methods are used to diagnose this condition. This study focuses on research conducted between 2021 and 2025 that analyzes, diagnoses, and grades prostate cancer based on histopathological images using machine learning and deep learning algorithms. In this context, the reviewed studies also include an analysis of findings related to preprocessing and feature extraction methods that may aid in prostate cancer detection, as well as the classifiers used. According to the findings of the reviewed studies, artificial intelligence-supported prostate cancer detection systems demonstrate high clinical performance and significantly improve the diagnostic accuracy of pathologists by enabling rapid diagnosis. The presented research findings indicate a need for comprehensive studies focusing on prostate cancer using histopathological images. The integration of artificial intelligence is transforming prostate cancer pathology from a traditional and subjective process into a data-driven and standardized framework. This systematic analysis of histopathological images will make significant contributions to future prostate cancer research, help achieve more reliable results in clinical decision-making processes, and lay the groundwork for personalized medicine.

title: Algorithmic design choices as determinants of health equity: a causal simulation study of healthcare resource allocation
desc: Background. Care management programs increasingly rely on prediction algorithms to decide which patients receive limited healthcare resources. Because these algorithms are typically trained to predict future healthcare utilization or cost, they may systematically underidentify patients whose care-seeking behavior is suppressed by structural barriers. Objective. To evaluate how three modifiable design choices (selection threshold, feature set, and training objective) affect allocation equity in care management targeting. Methods. We constructed an analytical cohort of 201,216 adults from linked electronic health record and participant survey data in the NIH All of Us Research Program (2017-2019). Three prediction models (logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost) were trained and evaluated under simulation conditions that varied one design choice at a time while holding the others fixed. Equity was assessed using false negative rate (FNR), equal opportunity difference (EOD), and allocation rate conditional on need (an access-independent benchmark based on self-reported general health status). We also applied Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition to identify which predictors contributed most to the Black-White allocation gap. Results. Prior utilization understated self-reported health burden among disadvantaged groups: 33% of Black and 32% of Hispanic participants reported fair or poor health, yet only 22% and 19% were classified as high utilizers. White participants showed the opposite pattern: 25% were classified as high utilizers, while only 19% reported fair or poor general health status. Under baseline design choices, all three models produced similar disparities, with uninsured participants showing the largest gap (EOD: -0.148). Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition identified prior outpatient visits as the dominant contributor to the Black-White gap in predicted allocation, with higher average emergency department utilization among Black participants partially offsetting the effect. Varying the selection threshold had little effect; disparities persisted across all thresholds. Feature set variation produced mixed and group-specific effects; removal of prior outpatient visits achieved near-zero Black-White EOD (0.001, AUC: 0.77), consistent with the Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition finding. title: FateDriver: Weakly supervised dual-view graph learning for transition-specific prioritization of candidate regulators in cellular reprogramming
desc: Cellular reprogramming supports regenerative medicine, yet the endogenous regulators of a specified source-to-target transition remain incompletely defined. Existing computational methods rank candidate regulators from network topology, trajectory dynamics, or cell-state labels, leaving unused the factors experimentally delivered to induce the transition. We present FateDriver, a weakly supervised dual-view graph neural network that jointly represents cells and genes from single-cell transcriptomes, treats the delivered factors as sparse gene-level labels, and ranks the remaining genes for a specified transition under a positive--unlabeled formulation. Across two OSKM datasets and one GMT dataset, FateDriver ranked first or second among six methods in recovering externally curated reference genes, exceeded a supervision-matched non-graph model despite weaker co-expression with the delivered factors, and achieved the highest recovery of protein targets of pluripotency-inducing chemical cocktails in both OSKM datasets. Holding either the source or the endpoint fixed yielded distinct candidate programs, including a DDX58--interferon axis associated with cells lacking endogenous pluripotency markers. Applying the same framework to candidate source--target pairs prioritized distinct candidate origins for two in vivo partially reprogrammed intestinal populations. FateDriver converts sparse experimental knowledge into transition-specific hypotheses for regulator prioritization from single-cell trajectories.

title: Translational maturity of artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography varies across cardiovascular diseases.
desc: [Frontiers in cardiovascular medicine] Electrocardiography is a widely available and low-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking. Seventy-seven publications informed the review. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes. AI-ECG has progressed furthest in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced-left-ventricular-ejection-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated workflow or diagnostic-yield benefits, whereas acute myocardial infarction rule-out has reached prospective multicenter diagnostic validation. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy screening has also advanced through international validation and prospective implementation. By contrast, occlusion myocardial infarction detection, prediction of occult or future atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, long-term heart-failure prediction, and cardiac amyloidosis remain primarily validation-stage or risk-enrichment applications. Across domains, broader adoption is constrained by label quality, calibration, transportability, operating-threshold selection, and limited patient-outcome evidence. AI-ECG is therefore best positioned as clinician-supervised decision support linked to explicit downstream testing and care pathways.

title: Interpreting graph neural networks reveals microbial association patterns in inflammatory bowel diseases
desc: Traditional machine learning models trained on gut microbiome abundance profiles can distinguish individuals with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from non-IBD individuals. However, their interpretation typically considers taxa in isolation, making it difficult to understand how associations between taxa contribute to predictions. Here, we inferred individual-specific microbial association networks from longitudinal metagenomics data of 106 individuals in HMP2/iHMP and used them to train and interpret graph neural network (GNN) models, which we compared with abundance-based models such as Random Forest (RF). Although RF achieved higher predictive performance (AUPRC ~0.59 vs 0.446), interpreting the GNNs revealed that their predictions relied on a densely connected module of co-abundant Bacteroidales species. Unlike the taxa prioritized by RF, these species were not differentially abundant between conditions. In an independent cohort, this module carried most of the predictive signal, and removing its associations reduced performance to near chance. These results show that coordinated association structure, rather than abundance shifts alone, is a feature of the IBD gut microbiome, and that interpreting GNNs can uncover such patterns that complement abundance-based analyses.

title: Advances in artificial intelligence for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis of neurological diseases: a systematic literature review.
desc: [Frontiers in human neuroscience] Brain imaging is central to the structural, functional, metabolic, and neurophysiological characterization of neurological disease, yet interpretation remains constrained by heterogeneity in acquisition, annotation, expertise, and clinical context. This systematic literature review evaluates recent artificial intelligence approaches for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis, with emphasis on methods, modalities, neurological diseases, diagnostic tasks, datasets, validation practices, and translational limitations. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and covered peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2020 through June 2026. Eight information sources were searched using database-specific terms for artificial intelligence, neuroimaging, neurological disease, and diagnostic analysis. The search identified 1,078 records; 236 duplicates were removed, 842 unique records were screened, 258 full texts were assessed, and 123 studies were included after a record-level eligibility re-audit. Heterogeneous evidence was synthesized narratively and by descriptive mapping rather than meta-analysis. MRI was frequently represented in the included studies and auxiliary mapping data; CT was commonly used in acute stroke and intracranial hemorrhage; PET supported selected molecular and differential-diagnosis studies; fMRI and diffusion imaging were used for network and white-matter analysis; and EEG extended the scope to neurophysiological diagnosis. CNN and three-dimensional networks were commonly reported, while attention, Transformer, graph, self-supervised, generative, multimodal, and foundation-model approaches appeared in selected recent studies. Stroke, dementia, and brain tumors were frequently represented, but heterogeneous populations, outcomes, and incomplete validation extraction precluded ranking diseases, modalities, architectures, or validation strategies. The evidence suggests movement from task-specific pattern recognition toward multimodal and context-rich decision support in selected settings, but it does not establish uniform methodological superiority or clinical maturity. Dependable translation requires patient-level data governance, transparent reporting, uncertainty estimation, independent multicenter testing, prospective workflow evaluation, and clinically meaningful endpoints.

title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS
desc: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

title: Circulating Biomarkers with Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Risk Assessment and Therapeutic Monitoring: Evidence, Limitations, and Translation.
source: PubMed · Therapeutics and clinical risk management
desc: [Therapeutics and clinical risk management] Circulating biomarkers, particularly cell-free DNA (cfDNA), are transforming contemporary medicine through their capacity to provide dynamic, minimally invasive assessments of disease dynamics. Their clinical utility has broadened substantially to include oncology, cardiovascular conditions, transplant monitoring, infectious diseases, and persistent inflammatory disorders. Nevertheless, the increasing complexity and volume of biomarker-related data pose substantial challenges, necessitating the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning methodologies for improved data interpretation, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making. This review presents a thorough examination of recent progress in the integration of circulating biomarkers with AI within therapeutic contexts and clinical risk management. It outlines the translational trajectory from molecular signatures to precision medicine, addresses present constraints, and explores prospective developments. The objective of this review is to serve as a systematic resource for both clinical practice and research, thereby promoting the evolution of personalized medicine through innovative, biomarker-driven strategies supported by AI.

title: LIMBER: A Hybrid RNA Foundation Model for Predicting and Understanding RNA Structure and Function
desc: RNA foundation models offer a promising route to decoding the relationships between RNA sequence, structure and function, yet how model shapes the acquisition and organization of biological information remains poorly understood. Here we introduce Layer-Interleaved Mamba-Bidirectional Encoder for RNA (LIMBER), a hybrid foundation model integrating bidirectional self-attention with selective state-space modeling, pretrained on 40.5 million non-coding RNA sequences. Through task-specific fine-tuning, LIMBER achieves leading performance on secondary-structure prediction and non-coding RNA classification benchmarks, while demonstrating strong transferability to translation-related tasks and RNA--small-molecule interaction prediction. Beyond model development, we establish a unified, task-agnostic framework to systematically evaluate and interpret the biological knowledge intrinsically acquired by RNA foundation models. This framework validates LIMBER's strong capabilities in recovering RNA structures and predicting mutational effects, while uncovering a hierarchical, task-dependent organization of different biological information across model layers. By further systematically training and evaluating a broad panel of model variants spanning model capacity, training duration and dataset size, we uncover distinct scaling behaviors across structural, evolutionary and functional capabilities. Together, these findings establish LIMBER as a versatile RNA foundation model and provide broader insights into how architectural design, internal representations and scaling shape the learning of RNA sequence-structure-function relationships.

MRI-based deep learning model for prediction of Ki-67 expression level in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
desc: [Abdominal radiology (New York)] Ki-67 expression is a valuable prognostic indicator in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA). This study aimed to develop a non-invasive Deep learning (DL) model based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and clinical data to predict Ki-67 expression preoperatively. Patients with iCCA between January 2020 and January 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Based on immunohistochemistry, patients were classified into high-expression group (Ki-67 > 50%) and low-expression group (Ki-67 ≤ 50%). After image acquisition, tumor segmentation, and preprocessing, a 3D-ResNet10 network was utilized for MRI feature extraction. A feed-forward neural network (FFN) was used for clinical feature extraction. Subsequently, the extracted image and clinical features were fused and fed into a lightweight classifier to perform Ki-67 level prediction. The performance of the DL models was evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and the area under the curve (AUC). A total of 117 patients were ultimately included (30 cases in the high-expression group and 87 cases in the low-expression group). The model based solely on clinical variables demonstrated limited predictive efficacy (mean AUC: 53.18 ± 14.60%). The model utilizing MRI features alone exhibited high specificity (86.14 ± 10.25%) but modest sensitivity. In contrast, the fused DL model significantly outperformed both individual models, attaining a mean AUC of 84.24 ± 8.82%, an accuracy of 87.17 ± 5.95%, a specificity of 93.07 ± 9.35%, and a markedly improved sensitivity of 70.00 ± 19.44%, yielding a robust F1-score of 73.42 ± 12.28%. We developed and validated a non-invasive DL model integrating contrast-enhanced MRI and clinical parameters that accurately predicts Ki-67 expression in iCCA, demonstrating superior diagnostic performance.

title: Bioactivity foundation model for hit identification and hit-to-lead optimization from sequence data
desc: Learning from large-scale bioactivity archives is complicated by heterogeneous assay readouts and differences in data reliability. Here we show that a model that predicts probability distributions over binding affinities from sequence data opens model training to vast and diverse troves of heterogeneous bioactivity data. We develop PSICHIC+, a bioactivity foundation model trained on approximately 82 million protein-ligand records using a distributional objective that preserves quantitative resolution while incorporating variation in data reliability. Given a protein sequence and ligand SMILES, PSICHIC+ predicts binding affinity in milliseconds. In zero-shot virtual-screening benchmarks without target-specific training data, it improves enrichment over regression- and classification-based approaches and performs competitively with leading structure-based methods. In lab-in-the-loop campaigns, distribution-guided acquisition improves recovery of high-activity compounds under fixed screening budgets. Combining PSICHIC+ with Boltz-2 improves hit-to-lead affinity prediction over Boltz-2 alone, with mean correlation approaching that of FEP+ on the evaluated benchmarks, without requiring high-resolution protein structures. These results support distributional learning as a scalable approach to using heterogeneous bioactivity data for hit identification and hit-to-lead optimization.

Thyroid biomarker biosensing: Nanomaterial-enabled electrochemical platforms, clinical translation, point-of-care technologies, and intelligent diagnostics.
desc: [Talanta] Thyroid disorders represent a substantial clinical burden, requiring reliable biomarker measurement for diagnosis, monitoring, and disease assessment. Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxine (T4), thyroglobulin (Tg), calcitonin (CT), and thyroid-associated nucleic acid biomarkers are important analytical targets. Although established immunoassays, ELISA, imaging, and cytological methods remain integral to clinical practice, limitations related to laboratory infrastructure, sample requirements, and workflow complexity have driven the development of alternative analytical platforms. This review focuses primarily on nanomaterial-assisted electrochemical biosensors for thyroid biomarker analysis, examining how nanomaterial properties, biorecognition strategies, and electrochemical transduction influence analytical performance. Metal and metal oxide nanoparticles, carbon nanomaterials, metal-organic frameworks, metal chalcogenides, MXenes, quantum dots, and molecularly imprinted polymers are discussed for their roles in signal amplification, interfacial charge transfer, selectivity, and sensor stability. Complementary approaches, including chemiluminescent, photoelectrochemical, optical, and other emerging sensing strategies, are also considered to contextualize the broader analytical landscape, particularly in relation to their implementation in commercial laboratory and point-of-care platforms for thyroid analysis. Seventy representative analytical and diagnostic systems are comparatively evaluated according to sensing technology, detection range, sample type, and assay time, together with their progression toward portable point-of-care devices, commercial analyzers, rapid diagnostic formats, and wearable platforms. Emerging artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches for signal interpretation, disease classification, and risk assessment are discussed. Challenges in nanomaterial reproducibility, bioreceptor stability, biofouling, matrix effects, fabrication, analytical standardization, external validation, and clinical translation are critically examined. The review identifies key analytical and technological priorities for translating thyroid biosensors from sensitive experimental platforms into robust, reproducible, and clinically relevant diagnostic tools.

Integration of biomarkers in common retinal neurodegenerative diseases: a comprehensive review.
source: PubMed · Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
desc: [Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society] Retinal neurodegenerative diseases (RNDs) are major causes of irreversible vision loss worldwide. RNDs majorly include age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic retinopathy (DR), and glaucoma. Despite their distinct etiologies, these conditions share convergent mechanisms of retinovascular ischemia, neuronal apoptosis, and chronic inflammation. Physiologically, the retina and optic nerve are direct extensions of the central nervous system, sharing embryological origin, glial architecture, and neurodegenerative mechanisms with the brain, positioning them as an accessible model system for studying both ocular and systemic neurodegeneration. The growing field of ocular biomarkers thus offers objective, quantifiable endpoints for early detection, disease monitoring, and therapeutic evaluation of RNDs by bridging structural, functional, molecular, and genetic dimensions of retinal health. This narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature published between January 2015 and May 2026, identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, on ocular biomarkers in AMD, DR, and glaucoma. Eligible studies reported original clinical or translational research assessing imaging, functional, molecular, or genomic biomarkers with quantitative associations to disease diagnosis, prognosis, or treatment response. Biomarker evidence is organized by domain to enable cross-disease comparison and integration, and each major biomarker is graded by clinical maturity, distinguishing routine clinical use, research validation, use as a clinical trial endpoint, and regulatory acceptance. Optical coherence tomography-derived retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in glaucoma and geographic atrophy area on fundus autofluorescence in AMD are the most established biomarkers in clinical care and trials, whereas disorganization of retinal inner layers and vessel density in DR, and dark adaptation and ellipsoid zone integrity in AMD, are well supported in research settings but not yet standardized for routine clinical use. Ocular biomarkers are reshaping precision ophthalmology, offering reproducible measures for diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic monitoring across retinal diseases. While several structural and functional biomarkers are nearing clinical adoption, standardized acquisition protocols, external validation, and regulatory qualification remain critical next steps. title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiogram Screening for Detection of Low Ejection Fraction in Routine Care: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
source: PubMed · Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
desc: [Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc] Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) is common and treatable but often undiagnosed, especially in early stages with non-specific symptoms. AI applied to standard ECGs offers low-cost screening for low ejection fraction (EF), yet its real-world impact on diagnosis remains unclear. A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs assessed AI-ECG screening for low EF in clinical practice. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261287652). Databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central, Google Scholar) were searched from inception to January 18, 2026, for RCTs comparing AI-ECG screening to usual care in adults without known heart failure undergoing routine ECGs. The primary outcome was new low EF (≤ 50%) confirmed by echocardiography. Secondary outcomes included echocardiography referral rates, positive predictive value, and cardiology referral rates. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects model. Three RCTs were included (two individual and one cluster) with 37,467 participants. After adjusting for clustering, AI-ECG screening significantly improved detection of new low EF diagnoses compared to usual care (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.64; p = 0.002; I2 = 0%), with a number needed to screen of 204. No significant difference was found in echocardiography referral rates (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.09; p = 0.55; I2 = 36%). The PPV of the AI tool ranged from approximately 20% to 34% across studies. AI-ECG screening added to routine care improves low EF detection without substantially increasing echocardiography referrals. These findings support AI-ECG for earlier LVSD detection in at-risk populations, though further validation across diverse AI platforms is warranted.

title: Support Vector Machine (SVM)-Based Review of RNA-RNA Interaction Prediction Methods.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] RNA-RNA interactions (RRIs) play a vital role in cellular processes including gene regulation, RNA editing, and translational control. Aberrant RRIs are increasingly recognized as contributors to cancer initiation, progression, and metastasis. Accurate computational prediction of RRIs therefore offers significant opportunities for cancer biomarker discovery, understanding tumor biology, and therapeutic target identification. Among machine learning approaches, support vector machines (SVMs) have been applied in RRI prediction due to their robustness in handling high-dimensional, nonlinear data and relatively small training datasets. This chapter reviews SVM-based methods for RRI prediction, highlights representative tools and strategies, and discusses current challenges and relevance to cancer application. Emerging trends that integrate SVMs with deep learning and experimental data augmentation are also outlined, pointing toward pathways for clinical translation.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Three-Dimensional Preoperative Planning for Total Knee Arthroplasty in End-Stage Knee Osteoarthritis​.
source: PubMed · Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
desc: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] Accurate preoperative templating for total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in patients with end-stage knee osteoarthritis (KOA) remains challenging, and the accuracy of conventional planning methods is variable. This preliminary, retrospective, single-center study evaluated the reliability of a robot-independent, artificial intelligence (AI)-based, three-dimensional (3D) preoperative planning system (AIKNEE) for predicting prosthesis size and component position in patients undergoing TKA for end-stage KOA. Twenty-eight knees from 24 patients with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3-4 KOA were included. The primary outcome was the agreement between the planned and implanted prosthesis sizes. Secondary outcomes included correction of the coronal hip-knee-ankle (HKA) angle, improvement in Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) knee scores, and early postoperative complications. The planned size matched the implanted size exactly in 53.57% of femoral components (15/28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 35.8%-70.5%) and 46.43% of tibial components (13/28; 95% CI, 29.5%-64.2%). Agreement within ±1 size was 85.71% for femoral components (24/28; 95% CI, 68.5%-94.3%) and 96.43% for tibial components (27/28; 95% CI, 82.3%-99.4%), giving an overall matching rate of 91.07% (51/56; 95% CI, 80.7%-96.1%). The postoperative HKA angle improved from 173.0° ± 3.9° to 178.2° ± 1.2° (P < 0.001), and the HSS score increased from 39.7 ± 2.2 preoperatively to 80.8 ± 1.3 at the 1-month follow-up (P < 0.001). No major early complications, including infection, dislocation, or deep venous thrombosis, were observed. Within this preliminary cohort, the AIKNEE system predicted prosthesis size with a reliability comparable to that reported for existing AI templating tools. Because the study was retrospective, single-arm, unblinded, and limited to 1 month of follow-up, these data characterize planning accuracy only and do not demonstrate clinical effectiveness; adequately powered, controlled studies with long-term follow-up are required.

title: Artificial intelligence attitudes, presenteeism, and work engagement among nurses: a structural equation modeling approach.
desc: [Frontiers in psychology] The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into healthcare has transformed clinical practice, yet the psychological mechanisms linking nurses' AI attitudes to their occupational functioning remain insufficiently understood, particularly regarding the role of presenteeism as a potential explanatory pathway. This study aimed to examine the relationships among nurses' attitudes toward AI, presenteeism, and work engagement, and to test the mediating role of presenteeism within a Job Demands-Resources framework. A cross-sectional correlational design was employed, with data collected from 806 hospital nurses across Saudi Arabia and Egypt using the AI Attitude Scale for Nurses, the Presenteeism Scale in Nursing, and the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale. Data were analyzed via structural equation modeling with bootstrapped mediation testing (2,000 resamples) and multi-group invariance analysis. Following the exclusion of four multivariate outliers, the final analytic sample comprised 802 nurses. The hypothesized model demonstrated good fit (CFI = 0.981, RMSEA = 0.068). AI attitude significantly and negatively predicted presenteeism (β = -0.366, p < 0.001) and positively predicted work engagement (β = 0.436, p < 0.001), while presenteeism negatively predicted engagement (β = -0.250, p < 0.001). Presenteeism significantly and partially mediated this relationship (indirect β = 0.092, 95% CI [0.065, 0.123]), with the model explaining approximately 33.2% of variance in engagement. Configural, metric, and structural invariance was confirmed across Egyptian and Saudi nurses. These associational findings suggest that more favorable AI attitudes are linked to lower presenteeism and stronger engagement, offering preliminary guidance for nursing management and healthcare digitalization policies pending longitudinal confirmation.

title: Advancing Perioperative Medicine With AI: Current Landscape and Research Priorities.
desc: [JMIR perioperative medicine] AI is increasingly being applied across the perioperative continuum. AI should be viewed as a technology that can reduce cognitive burden, collate fragmented data into clinically meaningful information, support decision-making, and extend precision education to clinicians and patients. This editorial accompanies the JMIR Perioperative Medicine webinar held in May 2026 and presents our perspectives-informed by our clinical experience-on where AI can assist perioperative clinicians and surgical patients, the evidence available today, what is still needed, and how clinicians can prepare to practice alongside AI tools. We consider opportunities in preoperative risk assessment and optimization; intraoperative intelligent decision support; emerging technologies, such as surgical digital twins; and postoperative recovery, monitoring, and prediction of clinical deterioration. Most AI applications remain early and require large-scale, prospective validation across diverse populations and resource settings. Realizing their potential also requires confronting substantial challenges, including limited and fragmented training data, the specialized models needed to interpret the large volumes of data captured in operative videos and during physiological monitoring, biases embedded in data and algorithms or biases inherent in human-AI interactions, and the determination of where human oversight is essential and where it is not feasible. When used responsibly, with human judgment remaining paramount, AI offers an unprecedented opportunity to advance perioperative care.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted spectral microbiology for rapid microbial identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction: advances, challenges, and future perspectives.
source: PubMed · Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease
desc: [Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease] Rapid microbial identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction are fundamental to precision diagnostics, effective infection control, and antimicrobial stewardship. Artificial intelligence-assisted spectral microbiology is increasingly being investigated to convert complex spectral and imaging data into rapid microbiological identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction outputs. This review critically examines the integration of AI with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry, Raman spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, ultraviolet-visible-near-infrared spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging, and automated colony imaging for microbial identification, strain discrimination, and AMR prediction. This work focuses on spectral preprocessing, feature engineering, machine-learning architectures, interpretability, validation, and clinical translation. Emerging evidence shows substantial potential to accelerate diagnostics while improving analytical precision and scalability. Nevertheless, dataset heterogeneity, instrument-dependent variability, limited external validation, and insufficient model transparency continue to constrain real-world adoption. Future integration of multimodal spectral, genomic, and clinical data could deliver robust, explainable, and interoperable diagnostic systems. It may support precision microbiology and antimicrobial-resistance surveillance, provided standardized acquisition, external validation, quality control, and uncertainty-aware interpretation are in place.

title: Americans' views about artificial intelligence in healthcare: 2022-2026.
desc: [Health affairs scholar] The healthcare industry is quickly adopting artificial intelligence (AI). Understanding Americans' views is essential in shaping how these tools are developed and implemented. The data presented here were derived from 16 national surveys of US adults extracted from the Roper Center iPoll database (January 1, 2022-June 24, 2026). This analysis reveals a significant equity issue: more than 4 in 10 Americans using AI for a health question did so, in part, because they could not access or afford care. It also reveals a gap between what Americans believe AI can do for the healthcare system and their trust in it for their care. Public concerns about AI are leading to legislative action at the state level, but this activity primarily focuses on oversight, accuracy, and privacy, not on the access gap driving AI use for many Americans.

title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.
desc: [Biomolecules & therapeutics] Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly localize and track animals, whereas open-source pose-estimation tools extend measurement beyond centroid tracking to body-part trajectories and fine motor patterns; paired with supervised classifiers, they have matched human scoring and exceeded some commercial systems. Technical accuracy alone does not establish behavioral construct validity or pharmacological validity. Unsupervised methods such as Motion Sequencing represent drug responses and disease-model phenotypes as structured changes in behavioral states rather than only as predefined endpoints, providing high-dimensional fingerprints of pharmacological action. Segmentation and tracking foundation models may reduce annotation burden but require validation across species, strain, sex, apparatus, and paradigm. AI agents may assist with literature review, code generation, analysis auditing, and figure production but must remain within transparent, human-supervised workflows. In behavioral pharmacology, pose estimation is established as a measurement method and emerging as a drug-effect endpoint, supervised classification and unsupervised segmentation are emerging, and foundation models and agents remain prospective. AI-enabled behavioral analysis can become a reproducible phenotyping layer for drug discovery and toxicology if researchers adopt open pipelines, rigorous validation, and reporting standards, rather than replacing one opaque measurement system with another.

title: Harnessing big data and artificial intelligence for personalized medicine: from multi-omics integration to clinical decision-making.
desc: [Personalized medicine] High-throughput technologies generate large and complex biological datasets that can challenge conventional methods of analysis and visualization. Artificial intelligence (AI) can support the analysis and integration of these datasets, provide new analytical approaches, and accelerate biological research. However, reliable AI applications depend on high-quality, consistent data. Technical errors, bias, and deficiencies in analytical methods can produce misleading findings and undermine reproducibility. AI-based approaches may help identify errors and improve data quality, but poor-quality or biased datasets, limited reproducibility, and concerns about privacy and ethics remain important barriers to their use in biological research. A literature search was performed in PubMed for papers published between 2015 and 2025. This review summarizes recent advances in AI for biological data analysis, including its main applications and potential benefits. It also discusses methodological, translational, and ethical challenges that may limit implementation. Particular attention is given to data quality and reliability, alongside the responsible use of AI in biological research and its translation to personalized medicine.

title: Next-generation analytical platforms for neurochemical sensing: from conventional biosensors to intelligent brain interfaces.
desc: [Talanta] Neurochemical sensing is central to understanding brain function, neurological disorders, and precision neurotherapeutics. Despite advances in electrochemical, optical, implantable, wearable, and genetically encoded technologies, current platforms remain limited by molecular selectivity, long-term stability, biofouling, complex data interpretation, and clinical translation. This review critically examines 83 representative studies encompassing nanomaterial-enabled electrochemical sensors, implantable and wearable devices, genetically encoded and CRISPR-engineered systems, AI-assisted analytical frameworks, and multimodal bioelectronic interfaces. Among the reviewed platforms, 68.7% were based on electrochemical or electrical sensing, whereas only 9.6% incorporated explicit AI/ML-assisted data analysis, indicating that intelligent analytical functionalities remain relatively limited. AI-assisted platforms have shown promising capabilities for signal discrimination, quantitative analysis, and enhanced analytical performance across diverse neurochemical sensing modalities, but their reported performance remains highly dependent on the sensing architecture, experimental conditions, and level of validation. Rather than providing a conventional technology-centered survey, this review establishes a unified framework for evaluating neurochemical sensing across five dimensions: molecular selectivity, spatiotemporal resolution, operational stability, intelligent data interpretation, and translational readiness. The reviewed evidence indicates a transition from conventional single-modality sensing toward integrated platforms incorporating multimodal detection and intelligent data interpretation, with adaptive and closed-loop interfacing emerging as future directions. By connecting advances in molecular recognition, functional materials, bioelectronics, and AI, this review identifies key design principles, persistent bottlenecks, and realistic priorities for translating next-generation neurochemical sensing platforms into reliable and clinically relevant intelligent interfaces.

title: Generative artificial intelligence literacy profiles differ in academic self-efficacy and subjective well-being among adolescents.
desc: [Frontiers in psychology] Generative artificial intelligence (AI) literacy is increasingly important for adolescents, yet variation in literacy across multiple dimensions and its associations with educational and psychological outcomes remain insufficiently understood. This study identified generative AI literacy profiles among Korean adolescents with generative AI experience (N = 3,959) using K-means cluster analysis based on information evaluation, communication, creative use, and ethical use. Two profiles were identified: Higher AI Literacy and Lower AI Literacy. The profiles differed primarily in their overall literacy levels rather than in qualitatively distinct patterns across the four dimensions. Adolescents in the Higher AI Literacy profile reported greater generative AI education experience and higher academic self-efficacy and subjective well-being than those in the Lower AI Literacy profile. Differences in academic self-efficacy and subjective well-being remained significant after adjustment for gender, school level, academic achievement, and economic status. These findings demonstrate meaningful level-based variation in generative AI literacy among adolescents with generative AI experience and suggest that such variation is associated with educational experience and academic and psychological outcomes. A person-centred perspective may complement variable-centred approaches and inform future research and educational approaches that consider differences in students' generative AI literacy levels.

title: Comparative evaluation of vibrational spectroscopy and deep learning for hierarchical authentication of collagen-based biological matrices.
source: PubMed · Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
desc: [Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications] The authentication of highly similar biological matrices remains a major challenge in analytical chemistry because weak and overlapping spectroscopic signatures often limit reliable classification. Here, we establish a comparative analytical framework to evaluate the performance of vibrational spectroscopy coupled with conventional chemometric and deep-learning approaches using donkey-hide gelatin (DHG) as a representative collagen-rich model system. In five-fold cross-validation of 60 authentic and counterfeit samples, linear discriminant analysis achieved accuracies of 81.7%, 96.7%, and 100% using SERS, FT-IR, and NIR spectra, respectively; the first two NIR principal components accounted for 90.0% of the spectral variance. NIR also enabled complete cross-validation classification of four animal-derived gelatins. For the more closely related E1-E4 commercial products, AggMapNet achieved approximately 99% accuracy, compared with approximately 80-90% for conventional models. For three E4 commercial grades, 157 of 160 samples were correctly classified, corresponding to 98.1% overall accuracy, and balanced accuracy of 98.0%. These findings show that conventional chemometric analysis effectively resolves broader differences in authenticity and animal source, whereas AggMap-assisted representation learning enables finer discrimination among closely related commercial products and product grades.
